President Trump is due back at the White House after campaigning in San Antonio for Republican

Isaias is now the first hurricane of the Atlantic season in its latest advisory.
The National Hurricane Center in Miami said Isaias has strengthened into a category one

The Minnesota man has jailed on federal terrorism charges for allegedly planning a mass shooting
at a major shopping mall, Matt Sepic, and Minnesota Public Radio has more.
The FBI arrested Shaikdun Mohammed after he allegedly bought a semi-automatic rifle and
200 rounds of ammunition from an undercover agent.
Investigators say the 18-year-old told an informant that he planned to attack the Mall
of America because he couldn't afford to travel to Somalia to fight with the Islamic State
Group.
Mohammed made an initial court appearance Wednesday following his arrest in a public
park.
The French government says it will pause the use of stun grenades in its policing of student
protests after a 15-year-old boy's hand was blown off.
The devices, known as sting-ball grenades, are meant to disperse protesters if police
are surrounded.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports they are banned in most European countries.
"In a speech to the nation, Prime Minister Sebastien Le Corneux said contrary to what
people are saying, the police do not have orders to confront the students and are trying
to use proportional force in a difficult context, but there's been anger over what many say
are overly aggressive police tactics."
Students and police faced off Wednesday in Paris for several tense hours outside an elite
university whose students have joined the high school movement.
The students chanted anti-police slogans from behind a barricade of trash bins until the
police charged with tear gas to eventually clear the street.
Eleanor Beardsley in Pierre News, Paris.
And you're listening to NPR News.
The 87-year-old Spanish woman whose eviction last month sparked protests across Spain has
died.
Maria del Carmen Abascal, known as Marie Carmen, became a symbol for renters struggling with
Spain's housing crisis.
She had been hospitalized since the eviction from her home of more than 70 years.
More than 4,000 plaintiffs across the country are suing drugmakers claiming serious harms
from GLP-1 drugs, as NPR's Yuki Noguchi reports.
Millions of Americans take these drugs, yet there isn't much reliable data about serious
side effects like sudden blindness, pancreatitis, and gallstones.
Osempics maker Novo Nordisk says serious conditions are exceedingly rare in clinical trials.
The Food and Drug Administration tracks side effect reports filed by doctors, patients,
or companies, and PR found about 2,000 cases of pancreatitis and 1,000 cases of sudden
blindness out of 190,000 GLP-1-related findings since 2024.
But those reports are unverified, and doctors often don't report because it's hard to be
sure the drugs caused the problems.
Yuki Noguchi, NPR News.
The Los Angeles Dodgers are returning to the National League Championship Series, advancing
with a 4-1 win over the Atlanta Braves in Game 4 of their Best of Five Division Series.
They'll play for the pennant against the winner of the other Division Series between the Milwaukee
Brewers and San Diego Padres.
The Dodgers are seeking to become the first National League team to win three straight
World Series titles.
I'm Jyle Snyder, NPR News.
